items.q: Do I need Root for silent background updates?
items.a: No. ApkUp supports Shizuku out of the box, which grants elevated PackageInstaller permissions on stock Android (Android 11+ via Wireless Debugging or ADB) without rooting your device. Optional Root (su) is also supported for users who already run rooted devices or want single-tap in-place rollbacks.

items.q: Does Google Play Store checking require my Google account?
items.a: No. ApkUp generates anonymous Play Store sessions directly on-device (no third-party dispenser server sees your requests) together with a privacy-minimized device compatibility profile (CPU ABI, Android SDK, density, and language) to fetch compatible updates without any personal login.

items.q: How does ApkUp protect me from tampered or incompatible APKs?
items.a: Before any installer runs, ApkUp cryptographically verifies APK Signature Scheme v2/v3 certificates against the installed app, validates SHA-256 digests and signed F-Droid indexes, blocks version downgrades, checks minSdk/ABI compatibility, and isolates .apkm extraction against Zip-Slip and decompression bombs.

items.q: Can I migrate my tracked apps from Obtainium or App Watcher?
items.a: Yes. ApkUp includes an interactive Obtainium JSON import preview (for app bindings, custom F-Droid repos, and watchlist candidates) as well as Obtainium JSON export and direct App Watcher watchlist import.

items.q: How do ApkUp self-updates and the Beta channel work?
items.a: ApkUp checks official GitHub releases (stable-only by default) and validates SHA256SUMS digests plus signing certificates before updating itself. Under Setup → About, you can opt into the Beta channel at any time and cleanly return to stable on opt-out.

items.q: Does ApkUp collect any analytics, crash logs, or telemetry?
items.a: Zero. ApkUp has no developer backend, no ads, no analytics SDKs, and no telemetry. First-launch source consent ensures zero network requests run until you choose your sources, and preferences/tokens are encrypted at rest with Google Tink (AES-256-GCM).

securityPage.title: Security Policy — ApkUp
securityPage.metaDesc: Supported versions, cryptographic APK signature & SHA-256 verification, and responsible vulnerability disclosure for ApkUp.
securityPage.lead: Complete security documentation based on SECURITY.md — covering supported versions, cryptographic verification, and responsible vulnerability disclosure.
securityPage.supportedLead: We actively provide security patches for the following versions of ApkUp:
securityPage.archLead: ApkUp enforces multi-layer verification across every update lifecycle stage:

pillars.title: Cryptographic APK Signature Verification
pillars.body: Before handing any downloaded APK or .apkm split bundle to PackageInstaller, Shizuku, or Root (su), ApkIntegrityVerifier verifies APK Signature Scheme v2/v3 signing certificates against the currently installed application and blocks certificate mismatches or version downgrades.

pillars.title: Signed F-Droid / IzzyOnDroid Indexes & SHA-256 Checksums
pillars.body: Repository indexes (entry.jar / index-v1.jar) are verified against pinned 64-hex SHA-256 X.509 signing certificate fingerprints, and downloaded APKs (including ApkUp self-updates via SHA256SUMS) are validated against expected SHA-256 digests.

pillars.title: Hardened Archive & Storage Isolation
pillars.body: All downloads reside in private internal app storage (cacheDir), .apkm split bundles enforce strict Zip-Slip and decompression-bomb limits, and cleartext HTTP traffic as well as cloud backups are strictly disabled.

pillars.title: Encrypted Credentials & Host Isolation
pillars.body: Local preferences and optional tokens are encrypted at rest using Google Tink (AES-256-GCM via Android Keystore). Authorization headers are pinned strictly to their target API hosts and stripped across cross-host redirects.

securityPage.disclosureBody: If you discover a potential security vulnerability within ApkUp (especially regarding APK signature verification, .apkm archive extraction, Shizuku IPC / optional Root su execution, credential storage, or network transport), please do NOT disclose it via public GitHub issues, discussions, or social media.
disclosureSteps: Use GitHub’s confidential Private Vulnerability Reporting.
Detail the issue, steps to reproduce, affected versions, and include a proof-of-concept if available.
We will review incoming reports promptly, investigate the scope, and release a patch before any public disclosure occurs.

googleLockPage.title: ⚠ Google’s 24h Sideloading Lock & Keep Android Open — ApkUp
googleLockPage.metaDesc: Detailed analysis & permanent unlock guide for Google’s 2026/2027 Android Developer Verification 24-hour sideloading lock, user impact, ADB/Shizuku workarounds, and Keep Android Open.
googleLockPage.h1: Google’s 24h Developer Lock & Keep Android Open
googleLockPage.lead: Android is facing the biggest restriction on sideloading in its history. Starting September 30, 2026 (pilot regions) and rolling out globally in January 2027, Google Play Protect blocks APKs from developers who have not submitted government ID and package keys to Google — forcing users through a hidden 24-hour Developer Options cooldown.
googleLockPage.checkerTitle: Am I Affected by Google’s 24h Lock?
googleLockPage.checkerQ1: 1. Device uses Google Play Services / Play Protect?
googleLockPage.checkerQ2: 2. How do you install ApkUp / FOSS apps?
googleLockPage.checkerResultAffected: ⚠ Affected: Complete the 4-step “Allow indefinitely” unlock below once.
googleLockPage.checkerResultAdb: ✓ Bypassed: ADB / Shizuku / Root installs bypass Play Protect’s 24h lock.
googleLockPage.checkerResultDeGoogled: ✓ Not affected: Devices without Google Play Services have no 24h lock.
googleLockPage.factsHeading: What Google Is Rolling Out — And When

facts.title: Pilot Enforcement Active
facts.body: Google Play Protect began enforcing mandatory developer verification in initial pilot countries (including Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand), blocking unregistered APKs by default.

facts.title: Global Play Protect Rollout
facts.body: Starting January 2027, Google Play Services pushes this restriction worldwide to certified Android smartphones — even for apps never distributed on the Play Store.

facts.title: Mandatory ID & Package Binding
facts.body: Independent authors must upload government ID, pay a registration fee, and bind every app’s package ID and signing certificate to Google’s central registry.

googleLockPage.whyHeading: From an Open Computer to a Locked Gatekeeper

whyItems.title: 1. You lose control over your own hardware
whyItems.body: You bought and own your smartphone, yet Google Play Protect decides remotely which software is allowed to run unless you jump through a 24-hour waiting hoop.

whyItems.title: 2. Chilling effect on independent & privacy apps
whyItems.body: Hobbyists, security researchers, students, and privacy-focused developers who cannot or will not hand over personal IDs to Google are automatically flagged as “unverified” and scary-blocked.

whyItems.title: 3. Friction designed to push users back to Play Store
whyItems.body: Real malware checks happen via cryptographic signatures and reproducible source code — not by hiding an off-switch in Developer Options with a 24-hour cooldown and a 7-day auto-reset trap.

googleLockPage.kaoBody: The Keep Android Open coalition documents the rollout, mobilizes developers and users worldwide, and raises awareness about open mobile ecosystems. Share the campaign or learn more on their site.
googleLockPage.impactTitle: What This Means for You as a User
googleLockPage.impactBody: Without unlocking Developer Options, tapping direct APKs from GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, or independent sites can be blocked by Play Protect. Once you select Allow indefinitely after 24h — or update via ADB, Shizuku, or Root (su) — ApkUp continues working without restrictions.
googleLockPage.unlockHeading: How to Permanently Unlock “Apps from unverified developers”
googleLockPage.unlockLead: Follow these exact 4 steps once per device to keep installing ApkUp and independent open-source apps without future blocks (click/tap each step to check it off):

steps.title: Enable Developer Options (7× Build Number)
steps.body: Open Settings → About Phone (on Samsung: Software information) and tap Build Number 7 times until Android confirms “You are now a developer!”.

steps.title: Toggle “Apps from unverified developers”
steps.body: Open Settings → System → Developer Options (or search for Developer Options in Settings), find Apps from unverified developers, and enable Allow apps from unverified developers.

steps.title: Confirm Lock Screen & Restart Device
steps.body: Verify your lock screen PIN, pattern, or biometrics when prompted, then restart your smartphone. The mandatory 24-hour cooldown timer starts immediately after reboot.

steps.title: After 24 Hours: Select “Allow indefinitely”
steps.body: Return to Developer Options → Apps from unverified developers once the 24 hours are up and choose Allow indefinitely.

googleLockPage.trapTitle: ⚠ Watch Out for the 7-Day Reset Trap!
googleLockPage.trapBody: Android offers a temporary 7-day option next to Allow indefinitely. If you select 7 days, Android automatically re-enables the lock after one week — forcing you to wait another full 24 hours. Always pick Allow indefinitely!
googleLockPage.trapRes7d: Day 1–7: Allowed → Day 8: ✕ Auto-locked again (+24h new wait!)

home.title: Overview & Quick Start
home.lead: ApkUp is a client-side multi-source Android app updater for Android 10–17 (API 29+). It checks, verifies, and installs updates across 7 ecosystems without telemetry or developer servers.

cards.title: Zero network calls before source selection
cards.body: On first launch, ApkUp shows an explicit Choose Update Sources dialog. Only the sources you enable are queried over HTTPS.

cards.title: Apps, Updates & Setup
cards.body: Manage installed User/System apps and Watchlist entries in Apps, run single or batch updates in Updates, and configure sources, schedules, and backups in Setup.

cards.title: Cryptographic signature & ABI guard
cards.body: Every downloaded APK or .apkm bundle is checked against the installed signing certificate, minSdk, and CPU ABI before installation.

cards.title: Requirements, languages & optional automation
cards.body: Runs on Android 10.0+ (API 29+) in 9 languages (EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, PT, RU, ZH-CN). Works via standard Android prompts or silently with Shizuku / Root (su).

steps.title: Choose your active update sources
steps.body: Enable F-Droid/IzzyOnDroid, GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, APKMirror, or Google Play Store in the onboarding sheet (adjustable anytime in Setup).

steps.title: Order source priority & optional pinning
steps.body: Drag and drop your preferred source order in Setup (e.g. GitHub → F-Droid → Play Store → APKMirror) or pin specific apps in Apps.

steps.title: Scan & update (interactively or silently)
steps.body: Pull to refresh in Updates, inspect release notes or save APKs via Detail, and install single apps or tap Install All.

sources.title: Update Sources, Repository Linking & Signature Protection
sources.lead: How ApkUp queries each source, how custom 3-way repository bindings work, and why signature mismatches occur when switching ecosystems.

cards.title: Global priority order with automatic fallback
cards.body: ApkUp evaluates enabled sources according to your drag-and-drop priority list. Pinning an app prioritizes that source first and falls back cleanly if no update is found there.

cards.title: Custom GitHub, GitLab & Codeberg / Forgejo links
cards.body: Bind any installed or watched app to owner/repo, multi-level GitLab subgroups (group/sub/project), or self-hosted GitLab/Forgejo instances.

cards.title: ABI matching, FOSS flavor & Regex filters
cards.body: Automatically selects arm64-v8a / armeabi-v7a / x86_64 assets over universal APKs, prefers FOSS/fdroid flavors when enabled, and supports custom asset Regex filters.

cards.title: Why Android blocks cross-source certificate changes
cards.body: Official F-Droid builds are signed by the F-Droid key, while GitHub/Play/IzzyOnDroid builds use the developer key. ApkUp detects mismatches before installation and still lets you Save APK.

tableRows.col3: Built-in FOSS mappings, custom owner/repo, SHA256SUMS self-updater

tableRows.col2: REST API v4 (gitlab.com & self-hosted + optional PAT)

tableRows.col3: Direct asset resolution with ABI & Regex filtering

tableRows.col2: Signed Index V2 (entry.jar) + Index V1 fallback
tableRows.col3: RFC 7396 incremental diffs, X.509 TOFU pinning, local-only matching

tableRows.col2: HTTPS API/Feeds + In-App Cloudflare WebView fallback
tableRows.col3: Direct .apk & .apkm split-bundle extraction with 10-min per-app cooldown

tableRows.col2: Direct on-device anonymous session (no Google login, no dispenser server)
tableRows.col3: Minimized device profile (ABI, SDK, density, locale) & HTTP 429 recovery

fdroid.title: F-Droid & Index V2 Repositories
fdroid.lead: ApkUp features a native F-Droid Index V2 engine with incremental RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch diffs, cryptographic JAR certificate verification, and 1-tap presets.

cards.title: Up to 95% less bandwidth on repeat scans
cards.body: Instead of downloading a 50+ MB full index every time, ApkUp verifies entry.jar and applies only the small JSON diff since your last check.

cards.title: Cryptographic fingerprint verification
cards.body: Repository JAR signatures are verified against their pinned 64-hex SHA-256 X.509 certificate fingerprint. Any tampered index or diff is rejected immediately.

deepDives.q: How to add any custom HTTPS F-Droid repository
deepDives.a: Open Setup → Update Sources → IzzyOnDroid / F-Droid → Add Repository. You can paste a full F-Droid share link including ?fingerprint=<64-hex> or leave the fingerprint empty on first add to let ApkUp verify the JAR signature and display the fingerprint for Trust-On-First-Use (TOFU) pinning.

tokens.title: Configuring GitHub, GitLab & Codeberg Personal Access Tokens
tokens.lead: Public repositories work out of the box without tokens. Adding a read-only Personal Access Token eliminates API rate limits (60 → 5,000 req/hr on GitHub) and enables batched GraphQL queries.

cards.title: GitHub Fine-Grained Token (Read-Only)
cards.body: Create a Fine-grained token at github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens with Public Repositories (read-only) — no write scopes needed. ApkUp verifies the token and shows your live remaining quota.

cards.title: GitLab & Codeberg / Forgejo Tokens
cards.body: For GitLab, create a Personal Access Token with the read_api scope. For Codeberg or self-hosted Forgejo, generate a read-only repository token in User Settings → Applications.

cards.title: Hardware-backed encryption & redirect stripping
cards.body: Tokens are encrypted locally with Google Tink (AES-256-GCM) in Android Keystore. ApkUp’s OkHttp interceptor strictly strips Authorization headers on any cross-host redirect (e.g. to CDN asset servers).

cards.title: Built-in Token Verification Sheet
cards.body: Tap Verify Token in Setup → Update Sources → GitHub / GitLab to confirm validity, account handle, and remaining API quota immediately.

shizuku-setup.title: Setting up Shizuku (Quick Guide)
shizuku-setup.lead: Shizuku is completely optional — standard Android installs work without it. Pairing Shizuku enables zero-touch silent background updates on stock, non-rooted Android 11+ devices.
shizuku-setup.stepsTitle: Wireless Debugging Setup (Android 11+ — No PC or Root Needed)

steps.title: Install Shizuku & enable Developer Options
steps.body: Install the official Shizuku app (from Google Play or GitHub) and tap Build Number 7 times in Android Settings → About Phone to unlock Developer Options.

steps.title: Pair Shizuku with Wireless Debugging
steps.body: Connect to Wi-Fi, tap Pairing in Shizuku, open Developer Options → Wireless Debugging → Pair device with pairing code, and enter the 6-digit code in the Shizuku notification.

steps.title: Start Shizuku & authorize ApkUp
steps.body: Tap Start in Shizuku, then open ApkUp → Setup → Installation & Automation → toggle Use Shizuku for background installs and tap Allow on the prompt.

deepDives.q: Alternative: Starting Shizuku via PC (ADB) or Root
deepDives.a: On Android 10 (or if you prefer USB debugging), run "adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/moe.shizuku.privileged.api/start.sh" from a PC. On rooted devices, simply choose "Start (for rooted devices)" inside Shizuku — or use ApkUp’s direct Root (su) installer toggle.

shizuku-deep.title: Shizuku & Background Installation (Architecture & Guards)
shizuku-deep.lead: Deep dive into how ApkUp orchestrates unattended background installs, Root (su) session fallbacks, Wi-Fi/charging guards, active time windows, and rollbacks.

cards.title: Elevated PackageInstaller Session via Binder
cards.body: After apksig v2/v3 and ABI checks pass, ApkUp streams the verified APK (or extracted .apkm splits) into an elevated PackageInstaller session via Shizuku Binder IPC or su pm install-create.

cards.title: Deferred self-update at the end of a batch
cards.body: When updating multiple apps including ApkUp itself, ApkUp installs all other apps first and schedules its own update last so the running worker is never killed mid-batch.

cards.title: Active hours, quiet hours & automatic catch-up
cards.body: Restrict background checks and auto-updates to an active window (e.g. 02:00–06:00 while charging on Wi-Fi). Deferred checks automatically catch up at the next allowed window.

cards.title: Automatic pre-update backups & 1-tap rollback
cards.body: When Rollback Backups are enabled, ApkUp archives the currently installed base + split APKs in private storage (up to 2 GB LRU) before installing the update.

deepDives.q: How in-place Root rollback (-r -d) vs. guided non-Root rollback works
deepDives.a: Android normally blocks version downgrades unless the app is uninstalled first. With Root (su), ApkUp can execute an in-place downgrade (pm install -r -d) keeping your app data intact where supported by the app. Without Root, ApkUp guides you through a clean two-step flow: uninstalling the newer build and immediately reinstalling the backed-up previous APK (or exporting it to Downloads).

obtainium.title: Obtainium Migration & Sync Guide
obtainium.lead: Seamlessly import your existing Obtainium app configurations, custom F-Droid repositories, and track-only watchlists into ApkUp — or export your custom ApkUp bindings back to Obtainium JSON.

steps.title: Export your JSON in Obtainium
steps.body: In Obtainium, open Import/Export → Obtainium Export to save your configuration JSON file (or test it offline first on our Source Checker page).

steps.title: Open Interactive Import Preview in ApkUp
steps.body: In ApkUp, navigate to Setup → Advanced Settings → Backup & Export → Obtainium Import and select your JSON file.

steps.title: Review matched bindings, F-Droid repos & Watchlist items
steps.body: ApkUp previews installed app repo bindings (GitHub, GitLab subgroups, Codeberg), custom F-Droid repositories, and uninstalled apps (which can be added to your Watchlist with one tap).

management.title: App Management, Watchlist, Filters, Schedules & Backup
management.lead: Master ApkUp’s day-to-day tools: Watchlist tracking for uninstalled apps, pre-release channels, 24-hour smart cache, SAF APK export, and full JSON backups.

cards.title: Track releases for apps before installing them
cards.body: Tap the + button in Apps to watch any GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, F-Droid, or APKMirror app without installing it yet, mark versions as Seen, or import lists from App Watcher.

cards.title: Selective Beta, RC, Alpha & Nightly support
cards.body: Keep your system stable by default and enable Beta, Release Candidate (RC), Alpha, or Nightly builds either globally or individually for specific apps.

cards.title: Instant retry without re-downloading & SAF export
cards.body: Verified downloads stay ready in private cache for 24 hours. Use Save APK in Detail to export single .apk files or bundled .apks split packages into Download/ApkUp/ or any custom folder.

cards.title: Portable settings & sanitized diagnostic logs
cards.body: Export all source priorities, pinned apps, hidden lists, custom repos, and schedules as a JSON backup (tokens are excluded for security), and export token-stripped .txt logs for debugging.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting Source Errors & Common Questions
troubleshooting.lead: Quick reference table for every network status code, rate limit, Cloudflare challenge, and package installer error — with direct solutions.

tableRows.col2: Unauthenticated GitHub IP rate limit (60 requests/hour) reached
tableRows.col3: Add a read-only GitHub Personal Access Token in Setup (raises limit to 5,000/h + GraphQL)

tableRows.col2: Anti-bot challenge or per-app cooldown active on APKMirror
tableRows.col3: Complete the automatic in-app WebView check or check Setup → Source Health & Cooldowns

tableRows.col2: Temporary anonymous Play Store rate limit
tableRows.col3: ApkUp automatically backs off and retries with a fresh anonymous session token

tableRows.col2: Expired, revoked, or malformed Personal Access Token
tableRows.col3: Open Setup → Update Sources → GitHub → Verify Token and replace or clear the token

tableRows.col2: Incomplete subgroup path or private repository without token
tableRows.col3: Enter the full group/subgroup/project path (plus read_api token for private repos)

tableRows.col2: Index JAR certificate does not match the pinned SHA-256 fingerprint
tableRows.col3: Check the official repository URL & ?fingerprint= before re-pinning in Setup

tableRows.col2: Update APK is signed with a different developer/F-Droid key than the installed app
tableRows.col3: Pin the app to its original source, or use Save APK and reinstall cleanly if switching ecosystems

tableRows.col2: Release asset requires a newer Android version or different CPU architecture
tableRows.col3: ApkUp blocks incompatible assets automatically to prevent broken install loops

tableRows.col2: Shizuku background service stopped after a device reboot or Wi-Fi change
tableRows.col3: Restart Shizuku via Wireless Debugging (or enable wireless auto-start on boot inside Shizuku)

sha256.title: SHA-256 Checksums & APK Signature Verification
sha256.lead: What SHA-256 checksums are, why they protect you from tampered downloads, and how to verify APKs on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.

cards.title: What is SHA-256?
cards.body: A 64-character cryptographic fingerprint of an APK file. Changing even 1 byte produces a completely different hash.

cards.title: APK Signature v2/v3
cards.body: Inside ApkUp, every update’s signing certificate is verified automatically against the installed app before installation.

sideloading.title: Installing Unknown Apps on Android
sideloading.lead: Step-by-step instructions for Android’s classic “Install unknown apps” permission plus power-user installations via Shizuku, ADB, and Root.

cards.title: Classic Android Sideloading
cards.body: Tap the downloaded APK, open Settings when prompted, enable “Allow from this source,” and install.

cards.title: Shizuku, ADB & Root (su)
cards.body: Use Shizuku (Wireless Debugging), adb install -r, or Root (su) for streamlined background installations.

google-lock.title: Google’s 24h Lock & Keep Android Open
google-lock.lead: How to permanently unlock Google’s 2026/2027 24-hour Developer Options cooldown (“Allow indefinitely”), why F-Droid criticizes ID verification, and the Keep Android Open campaign.

cards.title: Google’s 2026/2027 Developer Options Flow
cards.body: Enable Developer Options (7× Build Number) → Allow apps from unverified developers → Restart → After 24h choose “Allow indefinitely”.

cards.title: FOSS, F-Droid & keepandroidopen.org
cards.body: F-Droid builds reproducible open-source APKs without forcing anonymous developers to submit government IDs to Google.

accessibilityPage.title: Accessibility Statement — ApkUp
accessibilityPage.metaDesc: Accessibility commitment, WCAG 2.2 AA & EN 301 549 status, Android TalkBack / Voice Access support, known limitations, and feedback process for ApkUp.
accessibilityPage.lead: ApkUp is designed for reliable operation with Android TalkBack, Voice Access, Switch Access, hardware keyboards, and screen magnification — both inside the Android app and on this website.
accessibilityPage.statusBody: Both the ApkUp Android application and the companion website target full conformance with WCAG 2.2 Level AA, EN 301 549, Android Accessibility Guidelines, and WAI-ARIA 1.2 (last full audit: November 24, 2026).
accessibilityPage.appLead: Verified across Updates, Apps, Setup, onboarding dialogs, bottom sheets, and system notifications:
appItems: Full Jetpack Compose semantics with descriptive contentDescription labels, grouped update cards, headings, and live-region status announcements for scans, queues, and downloads.
WCAG 2.5.3 Label-in-Name consistency for Voice Access and click/custom-action alternatives for pull-to-refresh, long-press batch selection, and drag-and-drop source ordering.
Minimum 48 dp touch targets on interactive controls, configurable large 2-column app grid (preselected in Accessibility theme), clean focus traversal, and keyboard-accessible bottom sheets.

Standard WCAG 2.2 AA Light and Dark Material 3 palettes (>= 4.5:1) plus a dedicated Accessibility AAA theme (>= 7.0:1) with offline solar sunrise/sunset switching, crisp 1.5 dp borders, and automatic Dynamic Color pause.
Respects Android reduced-motion settings cleanly across animations, shimmer loaders, and visual effects.
accessibilityPage.webLead: Built with semantic HTML5 and zero-dependency native ARIA controls across all 9 locales:
webItems: Semantic landmarks, skip-to-content navigation, keyboard-accessible menus/tabs/dialogs, and visible 3 px focus indicators.
Pauseable screenshot showcase respecting prefers-reduced-motion alongside keyboard-triggerable image zoom and focus restoration on dialog close.
Three-way theme toggle (Dark, Light, and WCAG 2.2 AAA >= 7.0:1 High-Contrast Solar mode) validated across text, accents, errors, copied badges, and borders.
Responsive layout reflow down to 320 px viewport width and 400% browser zoom without horizontal scrolling traps.
Localized interfaces across 9 languages with accurate document and section lang attributes and keyboard-scrollable code and comparison tables.
accessibilityPage.limitsBody: Third-party release notes fetched dynamically from upstream repositories (such as GitHub or GitLab releases) are authored by external developers and may contain varying formatting. Android OS system prompts (Developer Options, Install unknown apps, and Shizuku pairing) depend on the device manufacturer’s system UI. Manual on-device TalkBack and Voice Access verification across Android OEM skins remains ongoing.
accessibilityPage.soloTitle: A Personal Note from the Solo Developer
accessibilityPage.soloBody: ApkUp is built by a single independent developer. I strive to implement every feature as accessibly as possible to the best of my knowledge and conscience — while continuously learning along the way. Accessibility across the app and website is an ongoing effort, and I am genuinely grateful for every single tip, hint, or helping hand from the community!
accessibilityPage.feedbackLead: Found an unlabelled button, keyboard trap, low-contrast text, or screen reader issue in ApkUp or on this website? Please report it directly on GitHub.
